title: Canonical logarithmic cotangent comparison and injectivity at a geometric point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $g:Y\to S$ and $h:X\to Y$ be morphisms of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, $y=ht$, and $A=\mathcal O_{X,t}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ the pointed-etale ring stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Use the actual relative logarithmic differential modules $D_X=\omega_{f,t}$ and $D_Y=\omega_{g,y}$, with their ordinary and logarithmic symbols [def-per-log-differential-stalk]. Put $I=\langle a\in A:a\notin A^\times\rangle$ and $k=A/I$, with its quotient map $\rho$; since $A$ is local, this is its residue field. Construct $C_Y=k\otimes_B D_Y$ without choosing a ring-stalk map as the quotient of $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}D_Y$ by the $k$-span of $\rho(\operatorname{germ}_v(k_0^\sharp a))\otimes q-1\otimes(\operatorname{germ}_w(a)q)$ for every pointed relative etale diagram $V\xrightarrow{k_0}W$ above $h$ with lifts $v,w$ satisfying $k_0v=w$, every $a\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ and $q\in D_Y$. Write $[1\otimes q]$ for its canonical symbols and put $C_X=k\otimes_A D_X$. Define $G\subset C_Y\times C_X$ to be the $k$-span of the pairs $([1\otimes d\operatorname{germ}_w a],1\otimes d\operatorname{germ}_v(k_0^\sharp a))$ and $([1\otimes d\log\operatorname{germ}_w m],1\otimes d\log\operatorname{germ}_v(h^\flat m))$, for all such pointed relative diagrams, regular sections $a$ and log sections $m$ on $W$. Define cotangent injectivity to mean $\forall q\in C_Y,\ (q,0)\in G\Rightarrow q=0$. When $f=gh$ as log morphisms, $G$ is precisely the graph of the canonical logarithmic cotangent comparison $k\otimes_B\omega_{g,y}\to k\otimes_A\omega_{f,t}$, so this predicate is its injectivity.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, the canonical map k(x) tensor Omega(X prime/Y) to k(x) tensor Omega(X/Y), referring to Kato (1988), 3.12. The balanced quotient and graph are the explicit construction of this map on the already defined logarithmic differential symbols.
